evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry catalogs oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal forms and reports several analyses: diverging strokes signifying separation in the Shuowen tradition; concrete gesture or object interpretations; 八 as an early graph for 分; and a proposal that the graph originally represented 別. It questions treating an abstract separation concept as a pictograph. These are competing proposals, not a settled account or a detailed chronology of stroke changes.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry cites oracle-bone uses as a cardinal numeral, including 八犬、八羊 (合集 371正), and in the month expression 八月 (合集 6). It also cites Western Zhou bronze numeral and ordinal uses, and a Warring States manuscript example. The cited oracle-bone contexts establish early numeral use; the page gives identifiers and period labels but not verified absolute dates for each inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry transmits 許慎's account: “別也。象分別相背之形。凡八之屬皆从八。” This documents the traditional interpretation that the graph depicts separation; it does not establish an earlier written separation use or prove the strokes depict a particular object.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字「八」字形演變
evidence.text: The character record lists forms in oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal script categories and presents a traditional separation/borrowing interpretation. The catalog supports the presence of those form categories, but by itself does not resolve the disputed origin or establish a stroke-by-stroke sequence.
evidence.title: 漢字「八」：字形演變

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1, via the reconstruction table
evidence.text: The table lists 八 ‘eight’ as Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *pˤret and Middle Chinese pet. These are reconstructions of the numeral word 八; they do not establish the pronunciation of a hypothesized source word meaning ‘separate’ or an object depicted by the graph.

evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin bā and Cantonese baat3, and reports Middle Chinese category 幫母、黠韻、入聲 with fanqie 博拔, plus Old Chinese labels in other reconstruction traditions. These are readings of 八, not independent evidence for the proposed source word's sound.

evidence.text: The entry reports Shuowen's separate graph analysis for 𠛰 and records separation-related senses for 別. It does not establish that 八 was a phonetic component in 別, nor that the earliest pronunciation of a proposed source word matched the numeral word 八.

gaps: The original referent of the two strokes remains unsettled; no inspected evidence establishes a particular depicted object or gesture.

The graph is traditionally explained as separation, and proposals connect it with 分 or 別, but no inspected source establishes a dated earlier written separation use before the oracle-bone numeral attestations.

The proposed whole-graph borrowing for ‘eight’ remains a hypothesis. The reconstruction *pˤret is for the numeral word 八; a corresponding system-specific reconstruction for the proposed source word was not established, so the sound match is unverified.
The dossier's Proto-Sino-Tibetan claims (*brat ‘cut apart’ and *pV-rjat ‘eight’) and Tibetan comparison were not verified from inspected specialist comparative-linguistic sources.
The broad gloss ‘all around/all sides’ has no dated semantic chain established by the inspected sources.
No component has a distinct origin_form in the article, so origin_relation remains none; 八 is treated as a whole graph, not a phonetic component within another graph.
